::: {#cor-odd-degree}
#### An even number of odd degrees

Every graph (@def-graph-vertices-edges) has an even number of vertices of odd degree (@def-degree).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Let $G = (V, E)$ be a graph,
let $O$ be the set of vertices of odd degree,
and let $N$ be the set of vertices of even degree.
By @thm-handshake,

$$
\sum_{v \in O} \deg(v) = 2 \card{E} - \sum_{v \in N} \deg(v).
$$

The right side is an even number minus a sum of even numbers, so it is even (@def-even-odd).
The left side is a sum of $\card{O}$ odd numbers.
Pair the odd numbers off two at a time.
The sum of each pair is even.
If $\card{O}$ were odd, one odd number would be left over,
and the left side would be an even number plus an odd number, which is odd.
So $\card{O}$ cannot be odd, and it is even.

:::

:::
